name: Starting grid (µm)
sentence: The size of the blocks proseg builds the starting cells from, and moves until iteration 200. Small: a start follows its outline. Large: a start reaches past it, over nearby RNA, a neighbour's too.
info: Made-up cells, started from cells only: a 3 µm band of neighbour RNA lies between their starting outlines. Proseg's defaults otherwise; each panel the middle of 27 copies. From iteration 200 (1 µm blocks, drift on) the difference mostly fades here. With 1 µm instead of 2 µm, one real cell's count of its neighbour's RNA fell from 20 to 8 (10 runs); on another real square proseg counted a quarter less RNA (3 runs).
spotTip: Bigger dots: the neighbour's own RNA lying in the gap between the two starting outlines, in the colour of the cell whose count keeps it.
statTip: Proseg's count of the pink dots in this panel: each adds the share of its gene this cell's count keeps, so a faint dot adds little. From iteration 200 every panel works on 1 µm blocks.
progressTip: Proseg's schedule: settling to iteration 200, refining to 400, final settling to 450. The panels show proseg's state every 5 to 50 iterations; the motion in between is drawn in. Nine copies share one 144 µm square, so edges move at about a real square's pace.
